::: {#rem-budget}

#### Spending a fixed budget

The sweep in @sol-rate-sweep trained `r nrow(py$sweep)` networks for 20 [epochs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch) each,
`r nrow(py$sweep) * 20` epochs in all.
One 100-epoch run of one network takes as many epochs as 5 of those trials.
Here, where training is not [compute-bound](#def-compute-bound),
the extra 80 epochs in @sol-longer bought nothing,
and the same 80 epochs would have paid for 4 more trials of the same [width](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-width),
such as more seeds or more [learning rates](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate).
When training is compute-bound,
@godbole2023playbook still advise against making every trial as long as the budget allows.
They tune in rounds,
starting with many short runs to find good settings
and ending with a few long runs at the best of them.

:::
